results.proposed_proof:
**Given:** A rational mixed Hodge structure $(H,W,F)$ with conjugation
$\sigma(h\otimes z)=h\otimes\bar z$ and conjugate filtration
$\bar F=\sigma(F)$, as in [[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]; the
complexified weight filtration $W_aH_{\mathbb C}=(W_aH)\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C$
is again written $W_a$.

[F1] On each $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}$ the induced filtrations $F$ and $\bar F$ are $n$-opposed, $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}H^{p,q}_n$ with $H^{p,q}_n=F^p\operatorname{Gr}^W_n\cap\bar F^q\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$, where $F^p\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$ is the image of $F^p\cap W_n$ and $\bar F^q\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$ the image of $\bar F^q\cap W_n$ ([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]], [[def-associated-graded-object-of-a-filtered-object]]).

[F2] $W$ is finite: $W_a=0$ for all sufficiently negative $a$ and $W_a=H_{\mathbb C}$ for all sufficiently positive $a$; $F$ and $\bar F$ are finite decreasing filtrations, so also the induced filtrations on each $\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$ are finite ([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]).

[F3] A finite sum of vectors lying in pairwise independent subspaces vanishes only if every summand vanishes; equivalently, the sum map from a finite direct sum of subspaces is injective ([[def-internal-direct-sum]]).



**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 (Two-filtration lemma, spanning and partial sums.) Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $\mathbb C$-vector space with finite decreasing filtrations $F$ and $\bar F$ such that $V=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}(F^pV\cap\bar F^qV)$ for an integer $n$. Then (i) $F^aV+\bar F^{n+1-a}V=V$ for every $a$, and (ii) $F^aV=\bigoplus_{p\ge a}(F^pV\cap\bar F^{n-p}V)$, with the conjugate formula $\bar F^bV=\bigoplus_{q\ge b}(F^{n-q}V\cap\bar F^qV)$. For (i), write $v=\sum_{p+q=n}v_{p,q}$; the terms with $p\ge a$ sum into $F^aV$, and each remaining term has $p<a$, hence $q=n-p>n-a$, that is $q\ge n+1-a$, so their sum lies in $\bar F^{n+1-a}V$. For (ii), prove $F^aV\subseteq\sum_{p\ge a}(F^pV\cap\bar F^{n-p}V)$ by descending induction on $a$: the claim is trivial when $F^aV=0$, and otherwise (i) with $a+1$ gives $V=F^{a+1}V+\bar F^{n-a}V$, so the modular law applied to $F^{a+1}V\subseteq F^aV\subseteq V$ yields $F^aV=F^{a+1}V+(F^aV\cap\bar F^{n-a}V)$, in which the induction hypothesis places $F^{a+1}V$ inside $\sum_{p\ge a+1}(F^pV\cap\bar F^{n-p}V)$ while $F^aV\cap\bar F^{n-a}V$ is the term with $p=a$; the reverse inclusion is clear, and the sum is direct because the pieces $F^pV\cap\bar F^{n-p}V$ are independent by the decomposition hypothesis, which is symmetric in the two filtrations, so the same argument with $F$ and $\bar F$ interchanged gives the formula for $\bar F^bV$. [given, algebra]

2.1 (Two-filtration lemma, vanishing.) Under the hypothesis of step 1.1, $F^aV\cap\bar F^bV=0$ whenever $a+b>n$. Indeed, let $x\in F^aV\cap\bar F^bV$ and let $x=\sum_{p+q=n}x_{p,q}$ be its unique decomposition with $x_{p,q}\in F^pV\cap\bar F^qV$. Since $x\in F^aV$, its decomposition lies in $\bigoplus_{p\ge a}(F^pV\cap\bar F^{n-p}V)$ by step 1.1 (ii), so $x_{p,n-p}=0$ for every $p<a$; since $x\in\bar F^bV$, the conjugate half of step 1.1 (ii) gives $x_{n-q,q}=0$ for every $q<b$. If $x\ne0$, some $x_{p,n-p}$ is nonzero, and it satisfies $p\ge a$ and $n-p\ge b$, whence $n=p+(n-p)\ge a+b>n$, a contradiction; so $x=0$. [step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 (Lifting.) Let $m=p+q$. Every $d\in W_{m-1}$ can be written as $d=z+g$ with $z\in F^p\cap W_{m-1}$ and $g\in(\bar F^q\cap W_{m-1})+\sum_{j\ge1}(\bar F^{q-j}\cap W_{m-j-1})$. To see this, construct elements $d_1,d_2,\dots$ and vectors $f_j,g_j$ as follows. Put $d_1=d$, and suppose $d_j\in W_{m-j}$ has been constructed for some $j\ge1$. By [F1] the induced filtrations on $\operatorname{Gr}^W_{m-j}$ are $(m-j)$-opposed, and step 1.1 (i) applied there with the pair $(p,q-j+1)$, whose indices sum to $m-j+1$, shows that the images of $F^p\cap W_{m-j}$ and $\bar F^{q-j+1}\cap W_{m-j}$ generate $\operatorname{Gr}^W_{m-j}$; choose $f_j\in F^p\cap W_{m-j}$ and $g_j\in\bar F^{q-j+1}\cap W_{m-j}$ whose classes sum to the class of $d_j$, and put $d_{j+1}:=d_j-f_j-g_j\in W_{m-j-1}$. By [F2] there is $J$ with $W_{m-J}=0$; the recursion stops there, and summing the identities $d_{j+1}=d_j-f_j-g_j$ gives $d=\sum_{j=1}^{J-1}(f_j+g_j)$. Each $f_j$ lies in $F^p\cap W_{m-j}\subseteq F^p\cap W_{m-1}$; $g_1$ lies in $\bar F^q\cap W_{m-1}$ and, for $j\ge2$, $g_j$ lies in $\bar F^{q-(j-1)}\cap W_{m-(j-1)-1}$. Hence $z:=\sum_jf_j$ and $g:=\sum_jg_j$ have the required properties. [F1, F2, step 1.1, construct]

3.1 (Surjectivity onto the graded summand.) Let $\xi\in H^{p,q}_m$. Since $H^{p,q}_m\subseteq F^p\operatorname{Gr}^W_m$ is the image of $F^p\cap W_m$, choose $x_0\in F^p\cap W_m$ representing $\xi$; since $H^{p,q}_m\subseteq\bar F^q\operatorname{Gr}^W_m$ is the image of $\bar F^q\cap W_m$, choose $y_0\in\bar F^q\cap W_m$ also representing $\xi$. Then $d:=x_0-y_0$ lies in $W_{m-1}$, so step 2.2 gives $d=z+g$ with $z\in F^p\cap W_{m-1}$ and $g$ in the displayed sum. Put $x:=x_0-z=y_0+g$. Then $x\in F^p\cap W_m$, and $x\in(\bar F^q\cap W_m)+\sum_{j\ge1}(\bar F^{q-j}\cap W_{m-j-1})$ because $y_0$ lies in the first summand and $g$ in the sum; so $x\in I^{p,q}$. Finally $x-x_0=-z\in W_{m-1}$, so $x$ and $x_0$ have the same class $\xi$ in $\operatorname{Gr}^W_m$. Hence the projection maps $I^{p,q}$ onto $H^{p,q}_m$, and $I^{p,q}\subseteq W_m\cap F^p$ holds by definition. [F1, step 2.2, algebra]

4.1 (Injectivity modulo the lower weight.) Suppose $0\ne x\in I^{p,q}\cap W_{m-1}$, and choose its least weight index $r$, so $x\in W_r\setminus W_{r-1}$ and $r<m$. Write $x=y+\sum_{j\ge1}g_j$ as in the defining formula, with $y\in\bar F^q\cap W_m$ and $g_j\in\bar F^{q-j}\cap W_{m-j-1}$; only finitely many terms are needed because $W$ is finite. Put $J=m-r-1\ge0$. The sum $\sum_{j>J}g_j$ lies in $W_{r-1}$, while $h:=y+\sum_{1\le j\le J}g_j$ lies in $\bar F^{q-J}$ and also in $W_r$, because $h=x-\sum_{j>J}g_j$. Thus the nonzero class of $x$ in $\operatorname{Gr}^W_r$ belongs to $F^p\operatorname{Gr}^W_r\cap\bar F^{q-J}\operatorname{Gr}^W_r$. But $p+q-J=r+1>r$, so step 2.1 makes that intersection zero, a contradiction. Together with step 3.1 this proves the projection isomorphism in (a). [F1, F2, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 (The weight decomposition and the direct-sum identity.) For every $m$ the projection restricts to an isomorphism $\bigoplus_{p+q=m}I^{p,q}\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_mH_{\mathbb C}$: by steps 3.1 and 4.1 each $I^{p,q}$ maps isomorphically onto $H^{p,q}_m$, and by [F1] the summands $H^{p,q}_m$ are independent with sum $\operatorname{Gr}^W_m$. In particular $\dim I^{p,q}=\dim H^{p,q}_m$, so $\sum_{p+q=m}\dim I^{p,q}=\dim\operatorname{Gr}^W_m$ for every $m$. The sum map $\psi_m\colon\bigoplus_{p+q\le m}I^{p,q}\to W_m$ is injective: if a finite sum $\sum_{m'\le m}\sum_{p+q=m'}x_{p,q}$ vanishes, its class in $\operatorname{Gr}^W_m$ is the sum of the classes of the top pieces $x_{p,m-p}$, which vanishes only if each of those pieces is zero because the restricted projection is an isomorphism; subtracting them leaves a vanishing sum over $m'\le m-1$, and induction on $m$ (with $W_m=0$ for all sufficiently negative $m$) finishes the argument. Its image therefore has dimension $\sum_{m'\le m}\dim\operatorname{Gr}^W_{m'}=\dim W_m$, the finite telescoping identity for the finite filtration $W$; an injective map between spaces of equal dimension is an isomorphism, so $W_mH_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q\le m}I^{p,q}$. Taking $m$ large gives $H_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p,q}I^{p,q}$. [F1, F2, step 3.1, step 4.1, F3, algebra]

5.2 (Conjugation modulo lower weights.) Work in $U=W_m/W_{m-2}$ with the images of $F^p\cap W_m$ and $\bar F^q\cap W_m$. Their intersection $T$ maps injectively to $\operatorname{Gr}^W_m$: its intersection with $W_{m-1}/W_{m-2}$ is $F^p\operatorname{Gr}^W_{m-1}\cap\bar F^q\operatorname{Gr}^W_{m-1}=0$ by step 2.1, since $p+q=m>m-1$. The formula for $I^{p,q}$ shows its image in $U$ lies in $T$, since every tail term has weight at most $m-2$. Step 3.1 shows this image maps onto $H^{p,q}_m$; the image of $T$ also lies in $H^{p,q}_m$, so injectivity makes the image of $I^{p,q}$ exactly $T$. Conjugating the same argument for $I^{q,p}$ shows that $\sigma(I^{q,p})$ has this same image $T$ in $U$. Therefore $I^{p,q}+W_{m-2}=\sigma(I^{q,p})+W_{m-2}$. [F1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 (The Hodge decomposition.) For all $a,m$ one has $F^a\cap W_m=\bigoplus_{p\ge a,\ p+q\le m}I^{p,q}$. Indeed, decompose $x\in F^a\cap W_m$ by step 5.1. Its class in $\operatorname{Gr}^W_m$ lies in $\bigoplus_{p\ge a}H^{p,m-p}_m$ by step 1.1, so its top components with $p<a$ vanish by the projection isomorphism. Subtracting the remaining top components leaves an element of $F^a\cap W_{m-1}$, and induction through the finite $W$ proves the assertion. Taking $m$ large proves $F^a=\bigoplus_{p\ge a}I^{p,q}$. Conjugating this identity gives $\bar F^b=\bigoplus_{q\ge b}\sigma(I^{q,p})$; it does not assert a decomposition of $\bar F$ by the original $I^{p,q}$. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 (Functoriality.) Let $f\colon H\to K$ be a morphism of rational mixed Hodge structures. Since $f$ is defined over $\mathbb Q$, $f_{\mathbb C}$ commutes with the conjugations, so $f_{\mathbb C}(\bar F^qH_{\mathbb C})=\overline{f_{\mathbb C}(F^qH_{\mathbb C})}\subseteq\bar F^qK_{\mathbb C}$; it also satisfies $f_{\mathbb C}(F^pH_{\mathbb C})\subseteq F^pK_{\mathbb C}$ and $f_{\mathbb C}(W_aH_{\mathbb C})\subseteq W_aK_{\mathbb C}$ by definition. Applying $f_{\mathbb C}$ to the two intersections and the sum defining $I^{p,q}(H)$ therefore produces an element of the corresponding intersection of $F^pK_{\mathbb C}$ with the sum of the $\bar F$-terms for $K$, and $W$-membership is preserved term by term; hence $f_{\mathbb C}(I^{p,q}(H))\subseteq I^{p,q}(K)$. [given, algebra] ∎

**Given:** A morphism $f\colon H\to K$ of rational mixed Hodge structures
([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]); the complexified map is written
$f_{\mathbb C}=f\otimes\mathrm{id}$ and commutes with the conjugations because
$f$ is rational.

[F1] The Deligne splitting of [[lem-deligne-splitting-of-a-mixed-hodge-structure]]: $H_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p,q}I^{p,q}(H)$ with $W_mH_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q\le m}I^{p,q}(H)$, $F^aH_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p\ge a}I^{p,q}(H)$, the projection of $I^{p,q}(H)$ onto $\operatorname{Gr}^W_{p+q}H_{\mathbb C}$ being an isomorphism onto $H^{p,q}_{p+q}$, and $f_{\mathbb C}(I^{p,q}(H))\subseteq I^{p,q}(K)$. The conjugation formula is only $I^{p,q}+W_{p+q-2}=\sigma(I^{q,p})+W_{p+q-2}$; no exact $\bar F$ partial-sum formula by the same pieces is used.

[F2] On $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}$ one has $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}H^{p,q}_n$ with $H^{p,q}_n=F^p\operatorname{Gr}^W_n\cap\bar F^q\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$ ([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]).



**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 (Weight strictness.) Let $y=f(x)\in f(H)\cap W_nK$ and decompose $x=\sum_{p,q}x^{p,q}$ along the splitting of $H_{\mathbb C}$; then $y=\sum_{p,q}f_{\mathbb C}(x^{p,q})$ with $f_{\mathbb C}(x^{p,q})\in I^{p,q}(K)$ by [F1]. Since $y\in W_nK=\bigoplus_{p+q\le n}I^{p,q}(K)$ and the sum is direct, all components with $p+q>n$ vanish: $f_{\mathbb C}(x^{p,q})=0$ whenever $p+q>n$. Hence $x':=\sum_{p+q\le n}x^{p,q}$ lies in $W_nH_{\mathbb C}$ and satisfies $f_{\mathbb C}(x')=y$, so $y\in f_{\mathbb C}(W_nH_{\mathbb C})$. The reverse inclusion $f(W_nH)\subseteq f(H)\cap W_nK$ is the preservation of $W$ by $f$. [F1, algebra]

1.2 (Hodge strictness.) The same computation with the condition $p<a$ instead of $p+q>n$: if $y=f_{\mathbb C}(x)\in f(H_{\mathbb C})\cap F^aK_{\mathbb C}$, decompose $x$ and use $F^aK_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p\ge a}I^{p,q}(K)$ to conclude that $f_{\mathbb C}(x^{p,q})=0$ for $p<a$, so $x'=\sum_{p\ge a}x^{p,q}$ lies in $F^aH_{\mathbb C}$ and maps to $y$. [F1, algebra]

2.1 (Rational descent.) Step 1.1 gives equality of the complexifications of the rational subspaces $A=f(W_nH)$ and $B=f(H)\cap W_nK$. Images and intersections commute with extension from $\mathbb Q$ to $\mathbb C$: in finite rational coordinates they are kernels or images of matrices, whose rank is unchanged on extension since the same nonzero rational minors remain nonzero. To descend $A_{\mathbb C}=B_{\mathbb C}$, map $A$ into the rational quotient $K/B$. Its complexification is zero, hence the rational map is zero (a nonzero rational coordinate remains nonzero over $\mathbb C$), so $A\subseteq B$; interchanging them gives equality. Together with step 1.2 this proves the stated rational $W$ strictness and complex $F$ strictness. Complex conjugation fixes the real scalar extension of a rational space and is not used to recover rational vectors. [step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

2.2 (Exactness of $\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$.) Let $0\to A\xrightarrow{i}B\xrightarrow{p}C\to 0$ be a short exact sequence of mixed Hodge structures. By [F1] the splitting identifies $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nA$, $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nB$, $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nC$ with $\bigoplus_{p+q=n}I^{p,q}(A)$ and its analogues, and the maps $\operatorname{Gr}^W_n i$, $\operatorname{Gr}^W_n p$ with the direct sums of the maps induced by $i$ and $p$ between the pieces $I^{p,q}$. Each piecewise sequence $0\to I^{p,q}(A)\to I^{p,q}(B)\to I^{p,q}(C)\to 0$ is exact: the middle arrows are the restrictions of the injective $i$ and of the surjective $p$, and an element $b\in I^{p,q}(B)$ lies in $\ker p$ precisely when $b=i(a)$ for some $a\in A$, and decomposing $a$ into its $I$-pieces shows that all other pieces map to zero; since $i$ is injective, they vanish and $a\in I^{p,q}(A)$. A direct sum of short exact sequences is short exact, so $0\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_nA\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_nB\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_nC\to0$ is exact; a morphism is strict for $W$ precisely when it induces such exact sequences, so this recovers step 1.1 independently. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 (Kernel, image and cokernel.) The functorial splitting [F1] makes $f_{\mathbb C}$ a direct sum of maps $I^{p,q}(H)\to I^{p,q}(K)$. Thus its kernel, image and cokernel decompose into the respective kernels, images and cokernels of these maps, and their induced or quotient $W$ and $F$ are the partial sums by $p+q\le n$ and $p\ge a$. The projection isomorphisms in [F1] identify their weight-$n$ pieces, with these induced $F$ filtrations, with the kernel, image and cokernel of $\operatorname{Gr}^W_n f$, computed componentwise in the pure decompositions $H^{p,q}_n,K^{p,q}_n$. These identifications are the canonical rational graded maps: for a kernel this follows from $W$ strictness, since if $f(x)\in W_{n-1}K$ with $x\in W_nH$, choose $y\in W_{n-1}H$ with $f(y)=f(x)$ and replace $x$ by $x-y$; the image and cokernel follow by the same induced/quotient description. The graded rational map commutes with conjugation and preserves $F$, hence also $\bar F$; between equal-weight pure structures it preserves each type $F^p\cap\bar F^q$ with $p+q=n$. Consequently its pure kernels, images and cokernels have conjugation exchanging their $(p,q)$ and $(q,p)$ pieces. Their $F$ partial sums and their conjugates are therefore $n$-opposed. Every weight-graded piece of the three rational filtered spaces satisfies the mixed Hodge axiom, proving the claim. This argument requires no exact conjugate decomposition on the mixed vector space. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 (Pure image.) Now suppose $W_{n-1}H=0$ and $W_nK=K$. By step 3.1 the image is a mixed Hodge structure with the induced filtration, and step 1.1 gives $W_{n-1}(\operatorname{im}f)=f(W_{n-1}H)=0$ and $W_n(\operatorname{im}f)=f(H)\cap W_nK=f(H)=\operatorname{im}f$; hence the image is pure of weight $n$. [step 1.1, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

**Given:** A rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex $K$ with its axiom: for
every $w$, $\operatorname{Gr}^W_wK$ has finite-dimensional cohomology, its
differential is strict for the induced $F$, and $H^r(\operatorname{Gr}^W_wK)$
with its induced $F$ and rational comparison is a pure Hodge structure of
weight $r+w$ ([[def-cohomological-mixed-hodge-complex]]).

[F1] The cohomological filtered complex construction: for a cochain complex with a decreasing filtration by subcomplexes, degreewise finite, $E_1^{p,q}\cong H^{p+q}(\operatorname{gr}^pK)$ and the sequence naturally abuts to the decreasing image filtration with $E_\infty^{p,q}\cong\operatorname{gr}^pH^{p+q}(K)$; a filtered chain map induces compatible maps on all pages and on the abutments ([[thm-the-cohomological-filtered-complex-construction]]).

[F2] Morphisms of mixed Hodge structures are strict, their kernels, images and cokernels with induced or quotient filtrations are mixed Hodge structures, and a morphism from a structure of weights at least $q$ to one of weights at most $q'<q$ is zero because its image would be both pure of weight $q$ and pure of weight $q'$ ([[lem-morphisms-of-mixed-hodge-structures-are-strict]]).

[F3] A cochain complex has $d^{n+1}d^n=0$, so its differentials preserve every subcomplex filtration used below ([[def-cochain-complex-in-an-abelian-category]], [[def-cohomological-mixed-hodge-complex]]).



**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 (First page and pure strictness.) Put $G^p=W_{-p}$ and apply [F1] over $\mathbb Q$ and $\mathbb C$. Then $E_0^{p,q}=\operatorname{Gr}^G_pK^{p+q}$, $E_1^{p,q}=H^{p+q}(\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-p}K)$ and $E_\infty^{p,q}=\operatorname{Gr}^p_GH^{p+q}(K)$ for the image filtration. The axiom gives $E_1^{p,q}$ a pure rational Hodge structure of weight $q$. We will use the following explicit pure case of [F2]: a rational map preserving $F$ also preserves $\bar F$; between pure structures of the same weight it therefore preserves each type $F^a\cap\bar F^b$, so it is strict for $F$, and its kernels, images and cokernels have the induced pure structures. If the source has weight $q$ and the target has weight $q'<q$, it is zero: a source vector of type $(a,b)$ with $a+b=q$ maps into $F^a\cap\bar F^b$ of the target, which is zero because no target type of total $q'$ has both indices at least $a,b$. Thus no mixed Hodge structure on the abutment is being assumed. [F1, F2, given, algebra]

1.2 (Strict representative correction.) For a complex $C$ with decreasing filtration $T$ by subcomplexes and $T$-strict differential, the sequence $0\to H^n(T^aC)\to H^n(C)\to H^n(C/T^aC)\to0$ is exact for every $a,n$. For injectivity, a cycle $x\in T^aC$ that is a boundary $dy$ in $C$ equals $dy'$ for some $y'\in T^aC$ by strictness. For surjectivity, a quotient cycle lifts to $x\in C$ with $dx\in T^aC$; strictness gives $y\in T^aC$ with $dy=dx$, so $x-y$ is a cycle with the same quotient class. If a cycle maps to a quotient boundary, subtract a lift of that boundary to obtain a cycle in $T^aC$, proving exactness at the middle. In particular $H(T^aC)$ identifies with the filtration induced on $H(C)$ by $T^a$. These corrections use only strictness of the differential on $C$. [F3, construct, algebra]

2.1 (Exact filtered pages through $E_2$.) Fix a Hodge index $a$, and apply [F1] with the intersection and quotient $G$ filtrations to $A=F^aK_{\mathbb C}$, $B=K_{\mathbb C}$ and $C=B/A$. Their $E_0$ complexes form a short exact sequence $0\to E_0(A)\to E_0(B)\to E_0(C)\to0$: the first image in $G^pB/G^{p+1}B$ is $(F^aB\cap G^pB+G^{p+1}B)/G^{p+1}B$, exactly $F^aE_0(B)$, and the last term is its quotient. The mixed Hodge complex axiom says $d_0$ on $E_0(B)=\operatorname{Gr}^GK_{\mathbb C}$ is $F$-strict. Step 1.2 therefore gives a short exact sequence on $E_1$, with first image exactly $F^aE_1(B)$. Naturality of the page maps shows $d_1$ preserves this image for every $a$; its rational form then makes $d_1:E_1^{p,q}\to E_1^{p+1,q}$ a map of pure Hodge structures of weight $q$, strict by step 1.1. Apply step 1.2 again to the $E_1$ complexes to obtain exactness on $E_2$, with $E_2(A)$ identifying with the filtration induced on $E_2(B)=H(E_1(B),d_1)$. Denote this recursively induced filtration by $F_{\mathrm{rec}}$. The pure type decomposition of $E_1$ descends through its type-preserving $d_1$, so $E_2^{p,q}(B)$ with $F_{\mathrm{rec}}$ is pure of weight $q$. [F1, given, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 (Higher differentials and exact stable pages.) Suppose the three page complexes are exact at page $r\ge2$, with $E_r(A)$ identifying with $F^a_{\mathrm{rec}}E_r(B)$ for every $a$, and $E_r^{p,q}(B)$ pure of weight $q$. Naturality shows $d_r$ preserves these images, hence $F_{\mathrm{rec}}$; it also preserves the rational structures. Its target $E_r^{p+r,q-r+1}$ has lower weight, so step 1.1 forces $d_r=0$. This zero map is strict, and step 1.2 applied to the exact triple of $E_r$ complexes gives exactness at $E_{r+1}$ and the recursive filtration identification. Since $d_r(B)=0$, injectivity of $E_r(A)\to E_r(B)$ and surjectivity onto $E_r(C)$ also give $d_r(A)=d_r(C)=0$. Starting from step 2.1 proves this induction for all $r\ge2$. Thus the weight sequence degenerates at $E_2$, and the three sequences for $A,B,C$ stabilize there; $E_\infty^{p,q}(B)=E_2^{p,q}(B)$ is pure of weight $q$ for the recurrent filtration. [F1, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 (Recurrent filtration equals the abutment filtration.) By convergence and naturality [F1], the injective stable-page map $E_\infty(A)\to E_\infty(B)$ is $\operatorname{Gr}_G H(A)\to\operatorname{Gr}_G H(B)$ for the image $G$ filtrations on cohomology. A filtered linear map between finite filtered spaces whose graded map is injective is injective and strict: for any nonzero $x$, choose its largest decreasing-filtration index $p$; its nonzero graded class has nonzero image, so the image has this same index. This proves injectivity and, if the image of $x$ belongs to $G^p$, forces $x\in G^p$, which is strictness. The cohomology $G$ filtrations here are finite in each degree because $G$ is finite on the degree-$n$ cochain group, so the argument applies to $H^n(F^aK)\to H^n(K)$. Consequently its graded image is the induced filtration of the subspace $F^aH^n(K)=\operatorname{im}(H^n(F^aK)\to H^n(K))$ on $\operatorname{Gr}_GH^n(K)$: in filtration degree $p$ the numerator is $(F^aH^n(K)\cap G^pH^n(K))+G^{p+1}H^n(K)$. By steps 2.1-2.2 that same image on $E_\infty$ is $F^a_{\mathrm{rec}}$. This proves exactly the recurrent-to-abutment comparison needed here, with the strict representative correction supplied in step 1.2. [F1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 (Mixed Hodge structure and shifted weights.) Write $W_mH^n(K)=\operatorname{im}(H^n(W_{m-n}K)\to H^n(K))$. Substitution $p=n-m$, $q=m$ in [F1] and step 3.1 gives $\operatorname{Gr}^W_mH^n(K)=\operatorname{Gr}^{n-m}_GH^n(K)\cong E_2^{n-m,m}$. Step 4.1 makes this identification compatible with the Hodge filtration induced by $F$ on cohomology; the right side is pure of weight $m$ by step 2.1. The rational comparison is an isomorphism on $E_1$ by the graded quasi-isomorphism axiom and hence on the stable pages; finite filtered leading-term descent makes it an isomorphism on cohomology as well. The finitely many nonzero stable terms in degree $n$ are finite-dimensional, so $H^n(K_{\mathbb Q})$ is finite-dimensional. The induced $W$ and $F$ are finite, and every $\operatorname{Gr}^W_m$ with its induced $F$ is pure of weight $m$, precisely the mixed Hodge axiom. [F1, given, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 (Functoriality.) A morphism of cohomological mixed Hodge complexes induces rational and complex cohomology maps compatible with the comparisons. It maps $W_{m-n}K$ to $W_{m-n}L$ and $F^aK_{\mathbb C}$ to $F^aL_{\mathbb C}$, hence preserves the cohomology image filtrations $W_m$ and $F^a$. These maps are therefore morphisms of the mixed Hodge structures of step 5.1. Naturality of [F1] and of the exact-page construction makes the graded-piece identifications compatible with these maps and their Hodge filtrations. [F1, given, step 4.1, step 5.1]

7.1 (The cosimplicial case.) Form $sK^n=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}K^{p,q}$ with the standard total differential. The cosimplicial identities, commutation with the internal differential and the usual total sign give $d^2=0$. The filtration $L_\ell sK^n=\bigoplus_{i\ge-\ell}K^{i,n-i}$ is increasing, by subcomplexes, and finite on each degree because $0\le i\le n$. Its graded piece is $\operatorname{Gr}^L_\ell sK\cong K^{-\ell}[\ell]$, so $H^r(\operatorname{Gr}^L_\ell sK)=H^{r+\ell}(K^{-\ell})$ is pure of weight $r+\ell$, and its internal differential is strict for $F$ by the Hodge complex hypothesis. Levelwise rational comparisons and filtration-preserving coface maps assemble to the total comparison, which is a graded quasi-isomorphism; the total complex is bounded below and its $F$ filtration is degreewise finite because each diagonal is finite. Thus $sK$ is a rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex for $L$. Applying steps 1.1-4.1 gives $E_1^{p,q}=H^{p+q}(\operatorname{Gr}^L_{-p}sK)=H^q(K^p)$, degeneration at $E_2$ and $\operatorname{Gr}^W_qH^n(sK)=\operatorname{Gr}^L_{q-n}H^n(sK)\cong E_2^{n-q,q}$, with its induced Hodge filtration and functorial mixed structure. Here $W_qH^n=L_{q-n}H^n$ is the shifted cohomology filtration, not the unshifted $L$. [F1, given, construct, step 1.1, step 3.1, step 5.1, step 6.1]

8.1 (Weights at most the degree.) Since the cosimplicial degree is nonnegative, $E_1^{p,q}=0$ for $p<0$, hence $E_2^{n-q,q}=0$ when $q>n$. Step 7.1 gives $\operatorname{Gr}^W_qH^n(sK)=0$ for all $q>n$; finiteness of the weight filtration then gives $W_nH^n(sK)=H^n(sK)$, proving the stated bound. [step 5.1, step 7.1, algebra] ∎
